bull.b: The PIPE financing and licensing proceeds materially extend Jasper’s ability to fund development without relying immediately on another capital raise. A runway through late 2028 supports execution of multiple clinical milestones and provides greater planning stability.

The Kira combination broadens Jasper’s pipeline beyond a single development program and creates several potential clinical value inflection points. Advancing assets across renal disease, PNH, SCID, and first-in-human development can diversify future approval and partnership opportunities.

Out-licensing two preclinical assets generates immediate funding while allowing another company to bear their subsequent development burden. Potential milestone payments preserve additional upside and demonstrate a pathway to monetize pipeline assets without fully abandoning them.

bear.b: Jasper has no commercial product revenue to offset its research and development costs, leaving profitability dependent on successful clinical development and future approval. Persistent losses also mean operating leverage is not yet visible and the business remains fundamentally pre-commercial.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow consumes resources before any product can generate recurring sales. Even with improved TTM burn versus 2025, continued dependence on external funding leaves Jasper exposed to financing conditions and execution delays over the development period.

The all-stock acquisition and convertible preferred financing substantially changed ownership economics for existing Jasper investors. Former holders’ small percentage of the enlarged company means future clinical success may accrue disproportionately to new Kira shareholders and PIPE investors.
